findings.description: You do not check if `fread` actually reads the expected number of bytes.
`ftell` and `fseek` can fail (e.g., on pipes or special files), and their return values are not checked.
If `filesize` is negative or extremely large, `malloc(filesize + 1)` can overflow, leading to buffer overflows or allocation of insufficient memory.
Printing the filename in error messages may leak sensitive information about the file system structure.
If the file is binary (not text), forcibly null-terminating may not be appropriate.
You pass `filesize` (not `filesize+1`) to `gcry_sexp_new`, so the null terminator is not used.
If `fread` fails, you do not free the allocated buffer before returning.
